# sh1x server wiki

Engineering wiki for this repository: hand-written pages about each subsystem,
plus a reference index generated by reading every C, C++ and assembly file in
`src/`, `tools/` and `tests/`.

Pages are editable in the browser by a signed-in editor, with a full revision
history. The reference half is read-only and rebuilt by a CLI command, because
the source is the truth.

```
wiki/
  content/            markdown pages that ship with the repo (seeded into the db)
  backend/            FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2 async + asyncpg
    app/indexer/      the lexical C/C++/asm scanner
    app/routers/      auth, spaces, pages, reference, search
    app/seed/         area descriptions and the content seeder
    tests/            indexer tests (pytest)
  frontend/           Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, hand-written CSS
  docker-compose.yml  postgres + backend + frontend
```

## Quick start (Docker)

```sh
cd wiki
cp .env.example .env          # set WIKI_SECRET_KEY
docker compose up -d
docker compose exec backend python -m app.cli bootstrap
```

Then open <http://localhost:3000>. `bootstrap` creates the schema, an `admin`
account, the source index and the seed pages. The admin password comes from
`WIKI_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, or is generated and printed.

The repository is mounted **read-only** into the backend container, so the wiki
can index the server source but can never write to it.

## Quick start (local)

Postgres must be reachable at `WIKI_DATABASE_URL` (the compose file publishes it
on `localhost:5433` by default).

```sh
cd wiki/backend
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m app.cli bootstrap
uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000

cd ../frontend
npm install
WIKI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 npm run dev
```

## CLI

```sh
python -m app.cli init      # create tables
python -m app.cli admin --username you
python -m app.cli index     # rebuild the source reference (~90s)
python -m app.cli seed      # load content/*.md  (--force to overwrite edited pages)
python -m app.cli stats     # what is currently loaded
python -m app.cli bootstrap # all of the above, in order
```

Re-run `index` after changing the server source. It replaces the reference
tables wholesale and never touches authored pages, revisions or accounts.

## Tests

```sh
cd wiki/backend && python -m pytest
```

## Configuration

Every setting is an environment variable with the `WIKI_` prefix, read from
`wiki/.env` (see `.env.example`):

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `WIKI_DATABASE_URL` | `postgresql+asyncpg://wiki:wiki@localhost:5432/sh1x_wiki` | Must use the asyncpg driver. |
| `WIKI_SECRET_KEY` | placeholder | Signs session tokens. **Change it.** |
| `WIKI_CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:3000,…` | Comma-separated. |
| `WIKI_REPO_ROOT` | the repository root | What the indexer reads. |
| `WIKI_CONTENT_DIR` | `wiki/content` | What the seeder reads. |
| `WIKI_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES` | `720` | Session lifetime. |

The frontend reads `WIKI_API_URL` (server-side only — the browser never calls
the backend directly; mutations go through `/api/proxy/...` so the session
token can stay in an httpOnly cookie).

## Adding a page

Either write it in the browser (**New page**), or drop a markdown file in
`content/` with frontmatter and run `python -m app.cli seed`:

```markdown
---
slug: subsystem-net
title: Transport
space: subsystems
summary: One sentence for listings and search.
position: 10
tags: [net]
---
```

A tag matching a source area name (`net`, `snapshot`, `player`, …) makes the
page appear on that area's reference page.

Seeding will not overwrite a seed page that has since been edited in the browser
unless you pass `--force`, which files the current text as a revision first.

## Note on the earlier prototype

`index.html`, `package.json`, `vite.config.js` and `scripts/sync-content.mjs` in
this directory are an earlier Vite/React prototype of the same idea. They are
superseded by `frontend/` and `backend/` and are not used by anything here; the
content-export approach they pioneered lives on in `backend/app/indexer/`.
